text.p: French catering group Sodexho, which on Tuesday announced that 1995/96 pre-exeptional profits rose 41 percent to 401.2 million francs, has forecast another strong performance for the current year.
It expected a 25 percent rise in pre-exceptional profit for 1996/1997 to around 500 million francs and company chairman Pierre Bellon was optimistic about the years ahead.
"(The) outlook is favourable," Bellon told reporters, saying he hoped for "good sales and profit growth in the coming years."
The company reported a 685 million franc net profit for 1995/96, reflecting an exceptional gain of 284 million francs related partly to the sale of its stake in Eurest.
"This performance is explained by an increase in sales, better operating margins and lower development costs," among other factors, Bellon said.

Consolidated sales rose 36 percent to 24.9 billion francs, of which 24 percent reflected the integration of British contract catering firm Gardner Merchant, acquired in February 1995. France and Great Britain and Ireland contributed nearly one half of sales.
Operating profit jumped 50 percent, reflecting the integration of Gardner Merchant, the company said.
Overall operating margins increased to 4.5 percent from 4.1 percent. The board boosted the net dividend to 26 francs from 22 francs.
